name: Carry-On Checklist
description: A carry-on checklist for packing a cabin bag, covering the liquids rule, essentials, electronics, comfort items, and what to keep on hand.

items.text: Travel-size liquids in a clear, resealable bag
Keep containers within the allowed size limit
items.note: Liquid limits vary by airport, so check current rules

items.text: Hand sanitizer within the size limit
Passport or ID and boarding pass
Wallet with cards and some cash
Copies of key documents stored separately
Power bank, kept in carry-on only
A book, e-reader, or downloaded entertainment
Snacks and an empty refillable water bottle
A change of clothes and clean underwear
Essential valuables, never in checked bags
Pen for arrival or customs forms

faq.q: What is the liquids rule for carry-on bags?
faq.a: Many airports limit liquids to containers of around 100ml, packed in a single clear, resealable bag. Limits vary by country and are changing in some places, so check your airport's current rules before you fly.

faq.q: What should I keep in my carry-on?
faq.a: Keep documents, money, medicines, electronics, valuables, and a change of clothes in your carry-on. If checked luggage is delayed, you still have the essentials to get through the first day comfortably.

faq.q: How is a carry-on checklist different from a packing checklist?
faq.a: A carry-on checklist focuses only on your cabin bag and the rules around it, while a packing checklist covers all your luggage. Use this for what flies with you and a packing list for everything else.

faq.q: Can I bring electronics in my carry-on?
faq.a: Yes, and larger electronics like laptops are usually safest in the cabin. You may need to remove them at security, and rules on power banks mean they belong in carry-on, not checked bags. Check your airline.
Yes. Print it or download the PDF, pack your cabin bag the night before, and confirm the liquids and electronics rules for your specific airline and route.
